afd.text:
000
FXUS62 KRAH 271913
AFDRAH

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
213 PM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

* No major changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES... 
As of 210 PM Friday... 

1) A brief warmup this weekend, with the next chance for rain late 
Sunday and Sunday night.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 210 PM Friday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1... A brief warmup this weekend, with showers expected 
ahead of a cold front late Sunday and Sunday night.

Aloft, a nrn stream s/w, which is expected to move onshore over the 
Pacific Northwest this evening, will track esewd across the Rockies 
and cntl Plains through Sat night. The s/w trough will amplify as it 
continues ewd across the Midwest on Sun, perhaps taking a slight 
negative tilt as it moves across the OH Valley, mid-Atlantic, and 
Northeast US late Sun into Mon. At the surface, a low pressure 
system will develop over the srn Plains Sat/Sat night, while high 
pressure moves ewd across FL. The low will then track ewd-newd 
across the mid-MS and OH Valley regions on Sun and the ern Great 
Lakes and Northeast Sun night/Mon. Meanwhile, a warm front should 
lift across cntl NC Sun aft/eve, immediately ahead of the attendant 
cold front, which should move ewd across the area Sun night. If the 
parent low begins to occlude as it tracks across the OH Valley/ern 
Great Lakes, a secondary triple point low may develop east of the 
Appalachians over wrn VA/NC, but confidence in that development is 
still somewhat low. There could be a brief window of some higher 
theta-e advection into the area Sun evening, but GFS forecast 
soundings still show little to no instability. However, the 
wind/shear profiles remain robust, with a rapidly strengthening low 
and mid-level jet over the area as the base of the trough swings 
across. The 12Z operational GFS has 40-55 kts at 925 mb and 65-75 
kts at 850 mb between 03Z and 09Z Mon. PWATs should also increase 
briefly to 1.2 to 1.5 inches NW to SE ahead of the cold front. For 
now, there is still a high probability for showers with minimal 
thunder potential, along and ahead of the front Sun eve through Sun 
night/early Mon. It may also be quite breezy, with the potential for 
some strong gusts if any deeper convection develops given the strong 
winds aloft. However, for now there is too much uncertainty/low 
confidence given the lack of instability and relatively weak low-
level lapse rates. The system should be fairly quick to move across 
the area, with rain ending by Monday morning, thus rainfall amounts 
should be limited, generally half an inch or less.

Temperatures: This weekend should be mild, with highs in the upper 
50s to mid 60s. Lows Sun night forecast in the 40s, based on current 
fropa timing, which is above to well above normal (5-15 degrees). A 
return to near to below normal temperatures is expected early to mid 
next week as high pressure builds into and sits over the region.


&&

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/... 
As of 1230 PM Friday... 

Cloud bases have been steadily rising to low-VFR with all sites 
expected to be prevailing VFR after 18z. Thickening cloud layer 
spilling across the mountains and into the Triad may result in brief 
MVFR cigs before clearing around or shortly after 06z. Steady 
southwest wind gusts will gradually weaken through this evening 
before becoming light around midnight. A strengthening LLJ and weak 
surface inversion will setup tonight into early Sat morning and will 
result in marginal LLWS (most near criteria at FAY/RWI), but with 
minimal change in direction through the lowest 2,000 ft will 
preclude its addition in the 18z TAFs. 

Outlook: Strong speed shear will likely result in LLWS early Sunday 
night ahead of a cold front. Ahead of a cold front, an accompanying 
band of rain, sub-VFR cigs, and gusty pre and post-frontal winds are 
all possible Sun night into Mon. 

&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...10
AVIATION...AS/Kren
